source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Omit PPE when a closed-system device is available because engineering controls eliminate all exposure risk","B":"Use a surgical mask alone because ventilation eliminates skin and mucous-membrane exposure to hazardous drugs","C":"Use ordinary examination gloves alone because chemotherapy-rated gloves are needed only for drug compounding","D":"Use chemotherapy gloves and a protective gown, adding eye, face, or respiratory protection as exposure risk requires"}}
source_row.rationale: NIOSH recommends chemotherapy gloves and a nonabsorbent protective gown for antineoplastic drug handling, with additional eye/face or respiratory protection according to the task and exposure risk. Engineering controls supplement rather than automatically eliminate PPE needs.
source_row.source_detail: Healthcare worker controls: chemotherapy gloves, nonabsorbent gown, and task-specific additional controls; Aug. 12, 2024 with 2026 hazardous-drug resources; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.source_name: CDC/NIOSH — Chemical Hazards Risk Factors: Antineoplastic Drugs
source_row.stem: A nurse administers an antineoplastic hazardous drug. Which PPE approach is most appropriate?
